newsitem.title: EGYPT: PRESS DIGEST - Egypt economic press - March 16.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Egypt economic press - March 16.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian economic press this week. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Investors are suffering from the central depository system. They complain of delays and increased costs but the registrars at the clearing house deny any responsibility for the slow procedures.

- Export Development Bank of Egypt is planning to set up a direct investment fund with a 150 million pound ($44 million) capital. The fund will not be open to the public but mutual funds and strategic investors can contribute to the capital. The fund is aimed at investing in public-sector companies the government is going to privatise and "closed" or rarely traded firms listed on the stock exchange.
- The clearing firm has devised a new system to finalise trades done by the mutual funds.

- Kafr el-Zayat Pesticides and Chemicals increased net after-tax profits for the first seven months of the financial year to 9.546 million from 3.486 million for the same period in the previous year. Net sales were 42.5 million compared to 38.85 million in the previous year.

- Central Egypt Flour Mills increased unaudited profits slightly for the first seven months of the year to 31.913 million from 31.422 million in the same year ago period. Revenues in the seven months ending January 1997 were higher at 365.917 million from 325.404 million in the same 1996 period.

- Nasr Dehydrated Agricultural Products unaudited profits for the seven months ending January fell to 275,000 pounds from 2.337 million in the same period of the previous year. Profits were lower due to the stiff competition the firm is facing in marketing its main product -- dehydrated onions -- in international markets.

- Abu Qir Fertiliser and Chemicals net after-tax profits for the first six months of the 1996/7 financial year rose to 117 million from around 90 million in the same period of the previous year. Net sales were about 302 million for the period ending December 31, 1996, up 16 percent.
- Chairman of Egyptian Financial and Industrial says in an interview that he expects net profits to be no less than 55 or 60 million for the 1996/7 financial year.

- Amriya Cement sharply increased pre-tax profits to 103.02 million for the seven months ending January from 83.47 million in same year ago period. Chairman Ahmed el-Meqati attributes the increase to reducing the number of shutdowns for maintenance to 16 days from 21.

- Egyptian Starch and Glucose ESGC.CA pre-tax profits fell slightly for the first seven months of the financial year to 20.480 million from 21.027 million in the same year ago period. A company official says the firm is targeting pre-tax profits of 34.7 million for the whole financial year as it bought large amounts of corn when international prices were low, lowering production costs.
- Holding Company for Housing, Tourism and Cinema offered the public at least 20 percent of its stake in partly-private Cairo Housing and Development.
- Arab African International Bank made a 6.0 million profit for 1996.
- A new, long-term wave of selling has depressed share prices between March 9 and 13.
- A new firm will begin to offer investors the facility to trade on the bourse by telephone.
- American Express Bank set up an open-ended mutual fund with a 100 million pound capital.
